sampling_model.design: Population identification from one pooled centered Gaussian mixture; the open statistical extension uses independent pooled draws.
sampling_model.units: Independent vectors \(Z_i\in\mathbb R^p\) when sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: A latent regime selects either the observational SEM or exactly one perfect stochastic intervention target.
sampling_model.overlap: Every component weight is positive; quantitative lower weight and separation requirements belong to Open-ended Question 1.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Population theorems recover the finite Gaussian mixture up to permutation; finite-sample covariance recovery is not assumed and is isolated in Open-ended Question 1.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 10 states that the observational context is exactly the unique minimizer of the deviation-rank score.
Theorem 1 gives sufficiency and worst-case necessity of one intervention per latent node for recovery under the paper's causal-disentanglement setup.
Theorem 4.1 learns mixture parameters efficiently when the number of components is fixed.
Corollary 4.1.1 identifies the interventional Markov equivalence class using mixture samples plus separate observational samples under interventional faithfulness.

Theorem 3.1 uniquely identifies the intervention tuples and their weights from a pooled mixture of perfect interventions on a given finite discrete causal Bayesian network under positivity and exclusion.
Theorems 1 and 3 recover intervention targets and certain parents from designated observational and interventional samples using sparse precision differences under intervention faithfulness.
Theorem 1 proves consistency of UT-IGSP for the interventional Markov equivalence class and unknown targets under interventional faithfulness with segregated regimes.
Theorem 6 characterizes the interventional Markov equivalence class as the sparsest distribution-equivalent graphs under faithfulness, intervention heterogeneity, and model truthfulness.
Theorem 1.1 clusters growing centered nonspherical Gaussian mixtures under near-disjoint total-variation separation with dimension-polynomial cost and weight-dependent factors.
Theorems 4 and 6 give effective-rank operator-norm moment and concentration bounds for sample covariance operators from labeled Gaussian samples.

body.tldr: An unordered pooled mixture containing one observational centered Gaussian SEM component and one effective perfect stochastic intervention per labeled node determines its entire semantic explanation without faithfulness. Coordinate-isolated precision pairs identify baseline-root pairs, invariant root marginals orient the baseline, and acyclicity makes the row-support target matching unique. These facts yield a sound-and-complete \(O(p^4)\) exact membership certificate, legal low-dimensional counterfamilies to the ICML 2023 rank selector, an open-family impossibility for all equivariant rank-only selectors, and deterministic recovery under operator error below \(\min\{\lambda/2,\alpha\lambda^2/16,g/8\}\). The end-to-end growing-dimensional component-estimation tail remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: The only published unknown-baseline reduction for this intervention geometry is Proposition 10 of Squires et al.; its decisive intervention-versus-intervention rank inequality is false, and its Appendix G concedes that rank at most two is only necessary for model membership. Kumar and Sinha identify pooled perfect-intervention components on a finite discrete causal Bayesian network only when the baseline network and observational law are given, under positivity and exclusion. Later Gaussian pooled-mixture work supplies observational data separately for causal discovery and invokes interventional faithfulness.
project_justification.niche: The observed-coordinate, centered, fully covered perfect-stochastic-intervention subclass has enough entrywise precision geometry to support universal identification at every legal parameter point, including unfaithful laws and nonroot interventions that preserve marginal noise variance.
project_justification.fill: The coordinate certificate recovers the baseline, target bijection, weighted DAG, structural and intervention variances, and mixture weights; it also certifies nonmembership, supplies a sharp information-loss diagnosis for rank-only selectors, and exposes the exact all-component margin needed for stable decoding.

body.related_work: Squires et al. (2023, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1) supply the causal-disentanglement setup and the precision-difference construction; their Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 is the theorem-level target replaced here, while Appendix G explicitly leaves complete membership testing open. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Definition 3.1, Assumptions 3.1 and 3.2, and Theorem 3.1) prove component and intervention-target identification for a pooled mixture of perfect interventions when the finite discrete baseline causal Bayesian network and its observational law are given, under positivity and exclusion. That theorem informs but does not subsume the present result because the observational component and baseline SEM are hidden here and must be recovered from centered Gaussian components. Kumar, Shiragur, and Uhler (2024, Theorem 4.1) motivate the pooled-mixture front end, but fix the number of components; their Corollary 4.1.1 additionally uses separate observational samples and interventional faithfulness, so it informs rather than subsumes the present semantic recovery theorem. Varici et al. (2021, Equation (6) and Theorems 1 and 3) provide the closest precision-support estimation machinery for a designated observational/interventional pair, but their diagonal screen and faithfulness-based guarantees do not select a hidden baseline. Squires, Wang, and Uhler (2020, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1) establish UT-IGSP for segregated regimes under interventional faithfulness. Gamella et al. (2022, Theorem 6) characterize a Gaussian noise-intervention equivalence class under faithfulness and additional conditions, rather than a hidden-baseline collection of perfect surgeries. Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025, Definition 1.5) supply identifiability terminology; their Theorem 1.6 gives higher-order-cumulant perfect-intervention recovery under a known observational context and non-Gaussian errors, leaving the centered-Gaussian hidden-baseline problem untouched. Anderson et al. (2026, Theorem 1.1) and Koltchinskii and Lounici (2017, Theorems 4 and 6) provide the two techniques named in the open statistical handle: growing-component centered-mixture clustering and within-cluster operator-norm covariance concentration.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact certificate is a real-arithmetic population procedure. It does not test approximate equalities, certify rational bit complexity, recover individual latent regime labels for pooled observations, or provide an end-to-end component estimator. The causaldag documentation for unknown-target IGSP expects separate observational and interventional sufficient statistics and regime metadata. On an accepted exact tuple, the certificate can supply the semantic baseline and target labels that such a workflow needs, and it recovers the DAG directly within its narrower model. It cannot by itself manufacture segregated samples or the empirical conditional-independence and invariance testers required by that software interface; it is therefore a semantic validation and initialization layer, not a drop-in statistical replacement.
body.honest_scope: The population identification, membership, rank-obstruction, and deterministic stability claims are all to be proved. The statistical component-recovery rate is intentionally open. The reduction at \(p=2\) agrees with the known directed-chain regression formulas; when \(G\) is empty, every support is a singleton and the certificate reduces to recognizing a diagonal baseline with one coordinate variance changed in each other component. At \(p=1\), the two variances admit both baseline orientations, so the restriction \(p\ge2\) is necessary. Missing interventions, soft or multitarget interventions, latent coordinate mixing, cyclic systems, and singular components are outside the positive theorem.
